You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Industry Solutions approach.

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: How SAP delivers its ~25 industry solutions for S/4HANA (industry-specific functionality, activation via business functions, examples: retail, healthcare, EC&O construction, professional services, industrial manufacturing), and what an industry layer needs to vary.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
YAML industry-template layer: terminology display overrides (Patient vs Customer, Job vs Production Order), chart-of-accounts preset, default tax codes, UoMs, enabled/disabled modules, typed custom fields (JSONB + metadata registry surfaced in forms, grids, report builder), approval presets, numbering formats; five shipped templates (manufacturing, retail, professional-services, healthcare, construction) applied idempotently at tenant creation.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

## SAP S/4HANA Industry Solutions & Enterprise Business Functions

SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management contains core functions for multiple industries, with extended industry functions found in the SAP S/4HANA Industry-Specific LoB Functions chapter.

### Business Functions in S/4HANA

Business Functions are technical switches in SAP ERP systems that SAP provided as new or additional features and enhancements in self-contained units for existing installations. However, while business functions may still be necessary to technically activate functionality in S/4HANA, they are no longer used as a licensing indicator.

### Commercial Structure & Industry Solutions

The basic commercial structure of SAP S/4HANA uses a business capability model consisting of three layers: Lines of Business, Business Areas, and Solution Capabilities.

Business function sets are classified according to industry, with at least one business function set for each industry containing all the business functions usable for a particular industry solution in one instance.

### Industry-Specific vs. Core Functionality

Core solution capabilities described in the "Enterprise Management" chapter are covered by the respective core license, while features in "Enhanced LoB Functions" and "Industry Specific LoB Functions" chapters require a separate license.

Based on the web search results, here's what I found regarding your query about S/4HANA's industry to core strategy, switch framework, business function sets, and irreversible activation:

## Switch Framework and Business Function Activation

The switch framework enables optional activation of business functions. With the switch framework, it's possible to control the activation of SAP ECC objects. Activating a business function triggers switches, which then influence the execution of the code enhancements.

## Irreversible Activation

An important constraint to note: You cannot undo the activation of a business function. This is a critical consideration when activating business functions in S/4HANA systems.

## Business Function Sets and Industry Classification

A business function set is nothing but a group of business functions. The business function sets are classified according to the industry. They contain functions specific to a particular industry and are part of the industry business function sets.

## Business Function Statuses and Conversion Constraints

Business functions can have the following status: always_on, customer_switchable, and always_off. If a business function is switched on in the start release system, but defined as always_off in the SAP S/4HANA target release, then a system conversion isn't possible with this release.

## Retail Activation

Regarding retail specifically, as of SAP S/4HANA 2022 FPS0, a new client-specific lightweight business function Fashion (RFM_FASHION) is introduced, that must be explicitly activated in all clients to get the functionality of fashion and vertical business.

The search results indicate that the switch framework is a proven mechanism for managing industry-specific and core functionality in S/4HANA, with careful consideration needed for the irreversible nature of business function activation.

input.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community/learning content, and ERP consulting sources, June 2026). SAP's S/4HANA industry approach folded most former IS add-ons into a single codebase ('industry to core'), covering roughly 25 industries whose functionality is activated per system through business function sets and the switch framework — activation is largely irreversible, one industry function set per instance, and industry-specific LoB functions are licensed separately from the Enterprise Management core. What the industry layer actually varies is substantial: terminology (Article vs Material, Site vs Plant), industry master data models (retail article/site, patient, equipment), entire vertical process suites (merchandise management, EC&O Equipment & Tools Management, professional-services Commercial Project Management, IS-U billing), regulatory content, and preconfigured SAP Best Practices content applied at setup. The current 2025/2026 direction adds a clean-core posture where deep vertical needs increasingly move to SAP Industry Cloud partner extensions on BTP — notably SAP is discontinuing healthcare IS-H by 2030 in favor of partner solutions. Atlas v1's YAML template layer maps well to the configuration-content slice of this area (terminology overrides, CoA/tax/UoM/numbering/approval presets, module toggles, typed custom fields) but plans none of the vertical process logic, industry master data objects, regulatory content, or partner extension ecosystem that practitioners associate with SAP industry solutions.
